coverage.note: Lectures 1-6. The 11 videos use 14 OCW decks whose numbering does not follow the videos; video 1 covers deck 01 alone, video 2 deck 02 alone plus its handwritten backprop-example deck, video 3 decks 03a and 03b, video 4 deck 04 alone, video 5 deck 05 alone, video 6 deck 06 alone.

images.format: whole slides rendered at 1400px, JPEG q85 or PNG whichever is smaller, named slide-N by PDF page number, or with a per-deck prefix (backprop-N, 3a-N, 3b-N) where a lecture has more than one deck
images.discovery: inline in wiki/ and raw/slides/; no index file
images.note: Lecture 1: 45 of 110 pages. Lecture 2: 15 of deck 02's 95 pages (slide-N) and 3 of the 14-page handwritten backprop example (backprop-N), in one directory. Lecture 3: 9 of deck 3A's 44 pages (3a-N) and 4 of deck 3B's 29 (3b-N), in one directory. Lecture 4: 16 of deck 04's 84 pages. Lecture 5: 7 of deck 05's 67 pages. Lecture 6: 8 of deck 06's 70 pages. Not rendered: slides with an OCW exclusion notice, slides that reuse an excluded figure without a notice (deck 3A slides 24-25; lecture 4 slide 77), superseded build steps and repeats, transcribed tables, unmarked third-party screenshots and logo graphics (lecture 5 slides 3, 4, 16), a figure already rendered for an earlier lecture (lecture 6 slide 3, lecture 5's slide 50), single-box text diagrams, logistics and text-only slides; the lists are in BUILD_LOG.md. No lecture after 6 is in this KB yet, so none has images.

caveats: Slide numbers are PDF page numbers. Some lecture 1 pages visibly print stale numbers from an older deck (page 13 prints 20), and lecture 2's deck prints N+1 from page 50 on; the slide files list them.

Catalog video titles misstate coverage: video 1 ends before training, video 2 shows only the four-line Keras model definition, video 3, titled for convolutional networks, never reaches them, and video 4, titled for transfer learning and Hugging Face, spends its first hour building CNNs from scratch.
Lecture 2's backprop example is a handwritten deck that the video points to but does not present; it is transcribed from the handwriting in its own slide file.
Figure checks were done by the parent model on rendered images, not by an independent agent.
Lecture 2 renders slides 55-58 and 69, which reproduce plots from a web page whose gradient-descent figures OCW excludes on slide 75 only; LICENSE.md names the source.
Lecture 3 spans two decks, cited as 'deck 3A, slide N' and 'deck 3B, slide N'; deck 3B prints N+1 from page 16 where it prints a number.
The course's Colab notebooks are not published on OCW. The Colab walkthroughs of lectures 3 to 6 are described from the lecturer's narration only.

Lecture 4 renders slides whose figures OCW does not mark as excluded but which credit third parties: deeplearning.ai (31, 32), Fig 14-2 of Hands-On Machine Learning (40), the CS231n notes (47), and screenshots of the TensorFlow, PyTorch and Hugging Face hubs (78-80); LICENSE.md names them.

Lecture 4's wiki page checks the Fashion-MNIST CNN's 302,000 parameters by its own arithmetic, under assumptions (no padding, pooling rounding down) that the lecture does not state; the page labels it as such.
Lecture 5's slide 63 prints copyrighted song lyrics; the slide file describes them and does not reproduce them.

Lecture 5's wiki page totals the song classifiers' parameters by its own arithmetic (40,035 and 160,035), extending the lecturer's 40,008 for the first layer under assumptions it names (a dense three-unit softmax output; a dropout layer with no weights).

Lecture 6 renders slides 49 and 51, a plot of GloVe word vectors that the deck does not credit and OCW does not mark as excluded; LICENSE.md says so. Its Cohere embedding quizzes (slides 14-19) and Chollet's figure (slide 47) are excluded and described in prose only.

Lecture 6's wiki page checks the frozen-GloVe model's 835 trainable parameters by its own arithmetic and counts the from-scratch model (320,547) under assumptions it names (a 5,000-word vocabulary and the same eight-ReLU and softmax layers); the lecture does not say which data split its accuracies (63%, almost 69%, 72%) are measured on.
